newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colonia says confident for 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Colonia says confident for 1997 profit.

text.p: German insurance firm CKAG Colonia Konzern AG said on Tuesday it was confident it would this year continue its good results of 1996, when net profits rose around 12 percent to 236 million marks.
In a letter to shareholders, the company also said Colonia's gross premium income in 1996 had risen 6.5 percent to 10.811 billion marks.

In a statement, Colonia had already announced plans to raise its 1996 dividend by a fifth, after profits in the year were boosted by increased internal efficiency, modest costs and claims and a strong investment performance.

Colonia pledged to continue its efficiency drive in 1997 and said economic conditions should improve somewhat over the year, although factors like Germany's record unemployment would mean a continued modest outlook for insurers.
"Overall we are confident that we will achieve a group result for 1997 that will continue from the good result of the previous year," the company said.
The insurer upped its 1996 dividend for common shares to 34 percent, or 1.70 marks, from 28 percent, while it raised its preferred share dividend to 36 percent, or 1.80 marks, from 30 percent.
Pre-tax profits rose around 10 percent to 444 million marks. Earnings per share advanced to 9.75 marks from 9.30 marks.
Colonia noted that some 230 million marks of the increase in its 1996 gross premiums was due to the first-time consolidation of units.
Growth in foreign business had also contributed disproportionately to the advance, with growth of 17 percent to 1.3 billion marks, or 12 percent of the total volume.
German insurers have generally been hampered in their domestic business by the sluggish economy.
The market leader Allianz last month reported a six percent rise in its 1996 premium income to 74.7 billion marks, but its German non-life business suffered a slight decline.
